Rathore also accused Rahul Gandhi of inciting unrest and mentioned foreign interference in India's stability.

stories.title: US midterms: Trump warns voters Democrats will 'destroy' America, backs Andy Biggs in Arizona governor race
China, Pakistan hold high-altitude army drills with Beijing-supplied arms
stories.summary: In a landmark move, China and Pakistan have kicked off their inaugural joint military exercise, dubbed Karakoram 2026, in the high-altitude region of Xinjiang. This operation emphasizes counter-terrorism strategies, utilizing advanced Chinese military technology. The participating forces aim to refine their skills in mountainous terrains, thus fortifying the strategic partnership between the two nations. The exercise promises improved synergy as troops navigate shared operational standards.

stories.title: SC Bar Association files criminal contempt plea against Sanjay Raut, Nikhil Wagle
stories.summary: Attorney General R Venkataramani has since granted consent to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against the two under the Contempt of Courts Act. The statements came after Chief Justice of India (CJI) declined a request last week from a delegation of opposition parties to meet him in person. The CJI said the delegation could instead file a petition before the court.

stories.title: ‘Big items are done’: Envoy Gor hints major boost in India-US trade negotiations
stories.summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor confirmed that negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement are advancing rapidly. Both sides have resolved major issues and are close to finalizing the agreement. Gor emphasized that the pace of negotiations is unusually swift compared to previous trade deals. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar also indicated that progress ensures a positive outcome is imminent.

stories.title: ‘Her misconceptions’: India rejects US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal’s remarks on voter rolls
After 50 years of fighting, Austin may secure Muny’s 141 acres while UT develops 190 acres nearby
stories.summary: Austin residents have passionately defended the historic Lions Municipal Golf Course for years, opposing potential developers. A new proposal seeks to officially hand over ownership of the golf course to the city, safeguarding its future. In return, the University of Texas would gain revised development regulations for neighboring properties on Lake Austin Boulevard. Officials assert that this arrangement effectively balances the need for green spaces with urban expansion.

stories.title: IGL rolls out AI system to check CNG cylinder safety at pumps
stories.summary: Indraprastha Gas Ltd has implemented an AI-enabled vehicle recognition system at various CNG stations in Delhi. This technology checks the hydrotest status of CNG cylinders to enhance safety measures. It ensures that vehicles with invalid certifications are alerted and refuelling is halted. The initiative follows a cylinder blast incident, prompting stricter enforcement of safety norms. The system will soon be deployed at all CNG stations managed by IGL.

stories.title: Renewable energy expansion needs to be aligned with transmission readiness: Experts
US temple attack plot: Teen’s alleged manifesto describes Indians as ‘subhumans’
stories.summary: A 19-year-old white supremacist's intention to attack a temple near Chicago was disrupted by a rifle malfunction. Following the incident, concerned colleagues notified authorities after he expressed his intentions via messages. Police arrested Alexandros Paporakis, uncovering alarming materials including a manifesto that targeted several communities. The case has raised serious safety concerns among Hindu organizations about worship places.

stories.title: Is Dhanush ready to make his political debut? Fan club's new avatar sparks buzz
stories.summary: Dhanush's fan club has evolved into the Dhanush Narpani Iyakkam, signaling possible political ambitions. The organization plans to set up local welfare units in five assembly constituencies within Coimbatore district. This transition involves the introduction of a new logo and flag, streamlining its identity. Although comparisons with Vijay's political path are inevitable, Dhanush has not made any official announcements regarding his political intentions, fueling speculation about his future moves.

stories.title: Families await return of 3 Indians killed in Germany fire; Kerala CM assures help with repatriation
Van Gogh’s hidden 1890 masterpiece resurfaces after 60 years, with a $180 million auction estimate
stories.summary: Vincent van Gogh's exquisite painting, Châtaigniers en fleurs, has resurfaced after being tucked away for over sixty years and will soon hit the auction block in New York. With an estimated value of around $180 million, this piece could shatter records. Once acquired in 1975, it has remained within the Blaquier family collection, drawing excitement from collectors, particularly during the recent preview in Hong Kong.

stories.title: In 2011, Florida's Michelle Parker vanished on the same day her engagement ring dispute was settled on reality TV. 15 years later, ex-fiancé arrested for murder
Delhi Police signals conditional nod for flag-waving, anthem at CJP's Oct 16 march amid curbs
In 2013, friends launched RXBAR with $10,000; Kellogg bought it for $600 million four years later
stories.summary: In 2013, aspiring entrepreneurs Peter Rahal and Jared Smith launched RXBAR while searching for nutritious protein bars. Starting from Rahal's parents' basement, they sold directly to customers. Their venture gained tremendous traction, culminating in a $600 million acquisition by the Kellogg Company in 2017, highlighting a significant trend towards clean-label snacks. Rahal remained CEO for two years post-acquisition before transitioning out.

stories.title: Brazil plants 840,000 trees to restore 607 hectares of Atlantic Forest
stories.summary: Brazil's Atlantic Forest is undergoing remarkable restoration efforts, spearheaded by World Land Trust and Reserva Ecológica de Guapiaçu. With 840,000 trees planted over 20 years, 607 hectares of degraded land have been revived into verdant forest. This initiative has created a vital wildlife corridor, facilitating the return of over 220 bird species to the previous wetland, while striving to protect and enhance the Guapiaçu watershed's remaining forest.

stories.title: 8-year-old Indian-origin girl dies of myocarditis after doctors missed warning signs; Australian coroner finds death preventable
Amit Shah vows to eliminate every trace of Naxalism after five decades of tribal suffering
stories.summary: Amit Shah highlighted the importance of eradicating Naxalism to restore growth in Bastar, Chhattisgarh. He noted that significant efforts had been made in this regard by local tribal leadership. Shah mentioned a distribution program of assistive devices benefiting over 3,600 disabled individuals, particularly Naxal violence victims. He emphasized the need to heal the wounds from years of suffering while maintaining that Naxalism's end does not restore dignity immediately.

stories.title: US not to livestream execution of Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan
stories.summary: Former US Army Major Nidal Hasan is scheduled for execution by firing squad on December 3, for the 2009 shooting at the US Army's Fort Hood base in Texas. Donald Trump stated that the execution will not be livestreamed, despite previous announcements from the Pentagon. Howevr, immediate family members of the victims may attend in person, if they choose.

stories.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on plea to hold protest organisers liable for damage
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has requested responses regarding a plea to hold protest organizers accountable for damages. This includes potential liabilities for loss of life, injuries, and property damage incurred during protests. Additionally, the plea advocates for designated protest locations to minimize disturbances in densely populated areas. It proposes that protest organizers disclose their funding sources to ensure transparency.

stories.title: France begins implementing agreement to protect Saudi oil facilities; what it means
stories.summary: France has started deploying military resources to Saudi Arabia to protect its oil facilities from regional attacks. This decision follows an agreement aimed at enhancing defense cooperation, especially amid increased drone and missile threats. President Emmanuel Macron confirmed the deployment, which includes soldiers and defense systems to bolster security. Recent attacks by Houthi militants have escalated tensions in the area, raising concerns for energy stability.

stories.title: Donald Trump is looking for a replacement of Susie Wiles; 'She's burned a lot of people': Report
J&K HC restricts motorboat operations on Dal Lake
stories.summary: The high court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh has ordered a ban on fuel-powered motorboats and jet skis on Dal Lake. Authorities are directed to enforce this prohibition strictly to protect the lake from pollution. The court suggested exploring solar-powered boats as an alternative for tourism-related activities. Emergency services and safety operations are exempt from this ban. A comprehensive policy on motorised boat operations is expected for further review.

stories.title: Bought in 2014, Magnolia’s Waco site grew from to 5.3 acres, adding shops, a ball field and church
stories.summary: In a remarkable transformation, Chip and Joanna Gaines have converted a historic cottonseed mill site in Waco into a buzzing tourist hub. Spanning 5.3 acres, the revitalized Magnolia property now features an array of shops, dining venues, and lush green spaces. Guests can experience restored historic buildings like the Old Church, while the newly built Katy Ballpark commemorates the original Katy Park.

stories.title: 'Stunned': Rahul urges President Murmu to put Dushyant Gautam’s appointment as Sikkim Governor on hold
Dhanush Narpani Iyakkam: Telugu star's fan club rebrands as welfare movement with new logo and flag
Zelenskyy claims jets hit: Ukraine says Su-34s struck with Neptune; vows long-range attacks continue
‘Please pretend I’m running’: Trump urges voters to back Republicans in US midterm elections
Meet Gabriella Rothberg, 17, who turned a sandwich idea into a patent for meat-flavoured tomatoes
stories.summary: A sandwich idea at 15 led Miami student Gabriella Rothberg to develop genetically engineered tomatoes designed to produce heme, an iron-containing molecule associated with meat flavour. Now 17, she is listed alongside her father on a US patent issued in June 2026. The project remains experimental, with taste and nutritional benefits yet to be established.

stories.title: Police shooting, water shortages, rising costs: Mauritius extends curfew amid unrest
stories.summary: Mauritius has extended a curfew for two additional nights after protests erupted over police violence. The unrest followed the shooting of a woman by a police officer in Camp Levieux, prompting increased tensions. Authorities reported over 100 arrests related to the disturbances and canceled school classes for security reasons. Anger over rising living costs and worsening water shortages has fueled public discontent across the island.

stories.title: IMD announces onset of winter monsoon in south Peninsular India, summer monsoon withdrawal completes on normal date
stories.summary: The southwest monsoon in India withdrew on schedule. Simultaneously, the northeast monsoon commenced, bringing rainfall to parts of south Peninsular India. Regions including Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and coastal Andhra Pradesh experienced the initial winter rainfall. Predictions indicate a normal winter monsoon may provide relief after a significant summer rainfall deficit.

stories.title: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal launches own party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
stories.summary: Divya Mittal, an ex-IAS officer, has established the Jan Neeti Bharat party in preparation for the forthcoming elections. With a focus on enhancing citizen participation in policymaking rather than adhering to conventional governance methods, she aims to make a significant impact. Her decision to retire after 13 years in civil service aligns with a trend of bureaucrats entering politics.

stories.title: 13-year-old Indian-American wins $25,000 for ocean acidification solution
EC announces Special Summary Revision of voters' list in 17 states amid SIR row
stories.summary: While a Summary Revision focuses on new eligibles and routine corrections, SIR goes far deeper, involving statewide house-to-house verification, detailed scrutiny of entries, and large-scale data audits. For instance, under a Summary Revision, a voter who has shifted homes must file a form to update their address. Under SIR, the Booth Level Officer visits that address, confirms whether the voter still lives there, checks if anyone new has become eligible, and updates the roll based on physical verification rather than waiting for the voter to initiate the change.

stories.title: President Murmu accepts L Murugan’s resignation amid buzz over Union Cabinet reshuffle
Evening news wrap: India seeks US probe into Illinois Hindu temple attack plot; BJP calls Rahul 'anarchic' & more
stories.summary: Men cheered outside a bathroom where a woman was reportedly being sexually assaulted at a Chicago party. India has called for a US investigation into a potential mass shooting plot against a Hindu temple. The BJP criticized Rahul Gandhi for undermining institutions during protests against the chief election commissioner. Congress questioned the government’s silence on Marco Rubio's planned visit to India.

stories.title: Akhilesh’s anti-BJP formula for UP: PDA, Muslim-Yadav votes and Gen Z
Lula or Bolsonaro: Why Brazil's presidential election matters for Brics and India
stories.summary: Brics began with five members and grew to eleven after the 2024 expansion, with Indonesia the newest, joining in 2025. Brazil opposed the enlargement, particularly because of the one nation. Iran. It feared that adding the avowedly anti-West Islamic Republic would cost the group its cohesion. Like India, Brazil wants Brics to be reformist and not revolutionary, thereby limiting it to a body that argues for change inside the existing order rather than one that tries to replace it.

stories.title: Ontario homeowner property listed for sheriff’s sale after $520,000 court order
Kumaraswamy slams Karnataka government over questioning of JD(S) workers
stories.summary: H D Kumaraswamy has voiced strong concerns about the Karnataka government allegedly targeting JD(S) members after a supposed sting operation. He reported that a party worker was detained at an undisclosed place without legal notice. Kumaraswamy staged a protest outside the police commissioner's office and expressed his willingness to be investigated, raising issues of biased investigations against opposition figures and social media actions.

stories.title: ‘Anarchic, immature’: BJP targets Rahul over anti-CEC protests; claims misconduct with women cop
Born with an underdeveloped arm, he built a LEGO prosthetic at 18 to help another boy
IISc, Samsung open quantum lab to advance research in next-gen technology
Missile heading towards Medina destroyed, says Saudi Arabia; Houthis deny attack
stories.summary: A missile targeting Saudi Arabia's Medina region was intercepted by the Saudi-led coalition according to their spokesperson. Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree refuted this claim, stating no operations were conducted towards Saudi territories. The ongoing conflict has resulted in a series of airstrikes from both the Houthis and coalition forces. Recent incidents include the destruction of a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh by the coalition.

stories.title: Washington uses helicopters to fly 6,000 logs into remote streams to restore salmon habitats
stories.summary: Helicopters are being used to deliver over 6,000 logs to remote streams in central Washington. The project aims to enhance salmon and bull trout habitats by creating pools and sheltered spaces. Log placement helps to retain water and slows down stream currents while allowing for better floodplain connectivity. The initiative is a response to past river management practices that greatly damaged these ecosystems.

stories.title: Severed head of Manipur attack victim recovered 5 days after Naga body’s discovery
Hollywood actress Pat Crowley’s Bel-Air home lists for nearly $16 million after more than 50 years; Howard Hughes once landed a plane nearby
Who is Holden Bierman? American teen who built a sustainable swimwear brand with $500
stories.summary: At just 12 years old, Holden Bierman founded Coastal Cool during the pandemic with a modest $500 loan. Originally selling casual apparel, he shifted focus to creating eco-friendly swimwear made from recycled materials. By partnering with Tidey Ocean, Bierman supports ocean plastic removal with every sale. While managing his business, he sacrifices typical high school experiences but aims to expand retail and study business at university.

stories.title: Wyoming ranch visited by Queen Elizabeth II hits market for $24.5M
stories.summary: The Quarter Circle Lazy B Ranch, spanning 1,542 acres in Wyoming, is now on the market for $24.5 million. This family-owned property has been in the Wallop family since 1889 and hosted notable guests like Queen Elizabeth II. The ranch features a luxury lodge, multiple homes, and retains its panoramic mountain views and tranquility. Accessible to the town of Sheridan, the ranch offers both privacy and outdoor recreation opportunities.

stories.title: 'SIR explain’: Smriti Irani turns Amitabh Bachchan movie scene into Rahul Gandhi jibe
Tampa Theatre turns 100: Historic movie palace reopens after $24.5 million restoration
stories.summary: Tampa Theatre has successfully wrapped up an extensive restoration initiative that commenced earlier this year. This project focused on revamping treasured decorations and upgrading essential infrastructure for future enhancements. A newly added education wing will support community-driven programs and classes, bolstering its cultural significance. Historical artifacts have been recovered and restored, ensuring the protection of its legacy.

stories.title: Hawaii’s Hā‘ena State Park reopens after 39 days following Hurricane Lowell
stories.summary: Hā‘ena State Park on Kaua‘i reopened on October 15 after being closed due to Hurricane Lowell. Visitors can now access specific hiking trails and Kē‘ē Beach, but restrictions remain. Overnight camping is still prohibited, while hiking beyond two miles along the Kalalau Trail is not allowed. Other state parks on Kaua‘i remain closed or have limited access due to extensive storm damage.

stories.title: What is causing the haze in Southeast Asia? Key facts explained
stories.summary: The ongoing wildfires in Indonesia have led to a sharp rise in respiratory issues across the region, significantly impacting air quality in neighboring countries like Singapore and Malaysia. This environmental crisis has caused escalating tensions as Indonesian officials feel mounting pressure to boost firefighting efforts and seek help from affected nations.

stories.title: 'Stop it, get lost': Chaos erupts at CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora's joint presser - video
stories.summary: Addressing the media, Dipke alleged that students and young people had been protesting in Delhi for the past 10-15 days and were being dragged away by authorities. He claimed that Opposition leaders who joined the demonstrations, including former chief ministers Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal and Pinarayi Vijayan, were also detained. “And all this for whom? For one man, Gyanesh Kumar,” Dipke said, referring to the Chief Election Commissioner.

stories.title: 'All for one man': CJP's Dipke targets Centre for sweeping curbs to stamp out anti-CEC protests
stories.summary: CJP activist Abhijeet Dipke has accused the government of detaining protesters for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He claimed that students and opposition leaders faced police action while protesting in Delhi. Rail services were reportedly suspended, and Metro stations were closed during the demonstrations. Neha Bora from All India Students' Association expressed her concerns about the treatment of journalists covering the events.

stories.title: Amelia Earhart vanished in 1937; a theory suggests crabs consumed her remains as a castaway
'Planned terrorist acts on behalf of Ukraine': Swedish national arrested in Russia
stories.summary: Russia’s FSB has detained a Swedish national accused of planning terrorist acts and sabotage for Ukraine. The agency claims he illegally crossed the border to execute these attacks on military facilities. Identified as Freddy Lindholm, he allegedly trained in drone operations after signing a contract with Ukraine’s army. His detention highlights Russian measures against foreign espionage amid ongoing tensions. The situation remains sensitive with varying international responses to the allegations.

stories.title: Erika Kirk pens emotional tribute to late husband Charlie Kirk on his birthday - video
Clint Eastwood saved a California ranch from condos; it became a 31-room hotel
Supreme Court issues notice on SIR petition, seeks records of EC decision-making
Oregon woman sold home to son-in-law, says he promised she could stay for life; court rejects claim
stories.summary: An Oregon woman who sold her home worth approximately $398,000 to her son-in-law for $270,000 in 2006 claimed she was promised the right to live there for life. After a dispute over her occupancy, a trial court ruled in her favour. However, the Oregon Court of Appeals overturned the decision, finding that the written sale documents transferred her entire ownership interest without reserving a life estate.

stories.title: US bank worker stole $280,000 and used fake reports to hide it
CJP's Dipke questions Imran Khan's 'Leave India' notice, cites Mary Millben's support for BJP
'Growing concern over anti-India hate in US': MEA demands probe into Hindu temple attack plot
stories.summary: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) has raised concerns about an alleged conspiracy aimed at a Hindu temple in the US. It called for a comprehensive investigation came following the arrest of Alexandros Paporakis in Illinois, accused of plotting a mass shooting driven at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois. Authorities uncovered alarming evidence tied to extremist views at his residence, leading the MEA to demand justice and advocate for community safety measures.

stories.title: 'Where anti-Indian hatred can lead': US lawmaker Raja Krishnamoorthi's warning after plot targeting Aurora Hindu temple
Chris Pratt and Katherine Schwarzenegger relist mansion for $19.99M, nearly $12M less
Jenny McCarthy co-hosted a pet contest; raised $8 million for 25-acre centre
Tony Parker’s Texas mansion vanishes from listings after price drops to $11 million
'Serious allegations': SC hears pleas on sexual harassment of women journalists, attacks on children among protest-related petitions
SC seeks Centre, Delhi Police response to plea challenging Jantar Mantar’s de-notification as protest site
Leh Apex Body condemns Chinese government over Ladakh remarks
UK man jailed for £10,000 fake single-father fundraising scam
Dhami government took steps at every level in Ankita Bhandari case: U'khand BJP chief
'Consistently sides with those who exploit women': BJP targets Congress over Akoijam's dismissal from JNU
Over 150 more 'Aam Aadmi Clinics' opened in Punjab: CM Bhagwant Mann
stories.summary: Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann dedicated 154 new Aam Aadmi Clinics to support healthcare initiatives across Punjab. He emphasized the significance of quality healthcare, education, and employment for all. Mann warned that changing the government could jeopardize public welfare programs like free bus travel for women. The new clinics are part of a larger commitment to accessible and affordable healthcare for families in need.

stories.title: 'Nobody can browbeat judiciary': SC issues notice to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and others over October 12 march
ACP Vivek Bhagat case: HC refuses urgent hearing on woman journalist’s arrest protection plea
'Open admission of regime change': BJP targets Rahul over Neha Bora's 'Bangladesh showed us the way' remark
SC upholds HC order denying OBC reservation benefits to Hindu converts to Islam
Sara Blakely invested $5,000 in Spanx while selling fax machines; 21 years later, it is worth $1.2bn
stories.summary: Sara Blakely founded Spanx in 2000 with $5,000 in savings while working as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson. Despite having no formal business training or outside investment, she built the company into a global womenswear brand. In 2021, Blackstone acquired a majority stake in the company at a $1.2 billion valuation, with Oprah Winfrey and Reese Witherspoon joining as investors.

stories.title: 'They silence voices of victims': Rahul, Kharge slam detention of Ankita Bhandari's parents
Katy Perry has supported UNICEF’s global child welfare efforts since 2013
Archaeologists find 19 injuries in 12 people buried in Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia
stories.summary: Archaeologists found evidence of traumatic injuries in 12 individuals from Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia. These injuries were discovered in domestic spaces like houses, pits, and wells across various sites. Examination of the remains revealed sharp-force and blunt-force injuries indicating potential violence in their lives. Researchers proposed that social conditions may have contributed to the unusual burial practices observed.

stories.title: Montana rancher’s rare Nanotyrannus fossil goes on display ahead of $9M auction
stories.summary: A rare find in the form of a nearly 70 percent complete Nanotyrannus skeleton, affectionately named Jodi, has been unearthed by rancher Jodi Pierson in Montana and is set to go under the hammer at Sotheby’s in New York on October 27. This well-preserved specimen is anticipated to garner between $6 million and $9 million, creating a buzz among paleontologists and collectors alike due to its invaluable significance.

stories.title: Once the fastest US liner, SS United States is set to become the world’s largest artificial reef
stories.summary: The historic ocean liner SS United States is set to be intentionally sunk off the coast of Florida, transforming it into the largest artificial reef in the world. This initiative follows successful environmental remediation and requires final approvals. To honor its legacy, a visitor center will be established, promoting tourism and attracting divers and anglers eager to explore this underwater attraction.

stories.title: Actor Imran Khan told to leave India by October 28 for protesting in Mumbai
Tech Aids Lost Birdsong Recovery: Synthetic calls help sparrows relearn old songs; scientists weigh AI’s role
stories.summary: A groundbreaking approach has emerged, leveraging computer-generated recordings to rejuvenate the bird songs that nature has lost. Researchers successfully reintroduced the unique call of the rufous-collared sparrow back into its habitat in Argentina. This innovative conservation strategy seeks to bolster endangered species by preserving their vocal heritage and fostering communication skills, as demonstrated by positive outcomes in captive breeding for species such as the regent honeyeater.

stories.title: 'Go to jail or be shot’: Trump warns US military secret leakers
stories.summary: Trump issued a warning to those leaking military secrets, suggesting jail or execution as consequences. He also discussed the bombing of Iran's nuclear facilities and threats against leakers. The Pentagon is planning a live-stream execution of Nidal Malik Hasan for his 2009 attack at Fort Hood. Trump confirmed support for this execution, emphasizing that he is indifferent to the method used.

stories.title: 'Can Hindus Eat Beef? BJP IT Cell Part 2': Dhruv Rathee faces two defamation cases in 24 hours
Oct 10 Jantar Mantar protest permission denied due to violence during CJP protest on Jul 20: Delhi Police
How opposition to data centres is bringing Democrats and Republicans together
‘Timely action’: India welcomes US response after Illinois teen held over Hindu temple attack plot
Con Edison’s $300M Bronx substation mimics a row of homes as $47.3M upgrade gets approval
stories.summary: Con Edison is set to invest $47.3 million in enhancing the East 179th Street substation in the Bronx. This vital upgrade will include the installation of a fifth transformer and a new feeder line. The initiative aims to bolster the local electric capacity, facilitating support for electrification and electric vehicles.

stories.title: NYC subway hides ventilation shaft and emergency exit behind 1847 Brooklyn townhouse façade
stories.summary: Nestled at 58 Joralemon Street in Brooklyn Heights lies a historic brownstone that harbors a subway ventilation shaft beneath its surface. Established in 1847, it transformed into a vital transit hub in 1908 under the Brooklyn Rapid Transit Company. The building's unchanged facade allows it to integrate seamlessly into the neighborhood while fulfilling crucial safety roles.

stories.title: Lake Ringgold Reservoir Permit: Judge overturns state approval; Wichita Falls weighs appeal
stories.summary: In a significant legal development, a Texas judge has scrapped the permit for the Lake Ringgold reservoir, amidst ongoing opposition from local ranchers concerned about environmental issues and property rights. Wichita Falls aims to appeal this ruling as they push for their water supply plans. This situation underscores the complex relationship between infrastructure advancements and conservation, with the city's next moves remaining unclear.

stories.title: ‘Stop protecting the VIP’: Ankita Bhandari's parents detained after overnight protest over governor appointment
Ukraine's drone ops slow after Musk's Starlink curbs as Trump warms to Putin
'Pakistan needs to look inwards': India questions UN rights body's silence on PoK unrest
How Chinese parts are fuelling Houthi ambitions to strike Israel and Saudi Arabia
Inside Meryl Streep’s former five-storey New York townhouse built in 1845
stories.summary: Meryl Streep’s former Greenwich Village townhouse, built in 1845, combines historic architecture with luxury features, including six fireplaces, six bedrooms and a rooftop garden. The three-time Oscar winner owned the five-storey New York property from 1995 to 2005. In 2016, it returned to the market with its asking price reduced to $28.5 million.

stories.title: 'White supremacist views': US teen held with rifle, ammo over Hindu temple attack plot
Microplastics found in 95% of UAE sea snakes across six species
Scientists create 3D models of USS Monitor, a Civil War ship 240 feet underwater
Jantar Mantar breach: Das, Ranka sent to 5-day custody
Government apologises to SC, says no wilful violation of its orders; measures were needed on Oct 10
Scientists detect quantum jumps in sound by tracking energy changes in real time
‘One Protest,’ says Rahul after arrest of CJP members; oppn vows to ‘reclaim’ Jantar Mantar
No cancellation of services, cut in metro train trips on October 10, SC told
SC: Cops can’t seek digital footprints for roving probe
Murdered Ankita Bhandari’s parents released from detention at 5am after overnight India Gate protest
BJP to take SIR counter-offensive to masses before polls
Won't accept lame excuses: SC to EC on 2023 case
SC: Tough PMLA bail conditions can't override accused's right
India to Starlink: Comply with rules before entering market
As Canada minister calls on him, PM Modi backs momentum in ties
India & US nearing a landing point on trade deal: EAM Jaishankar
India working on China ties, says Piyush Goyal
Underground detector records unexplained particle interaction in dark matter hunt
stories.summary: Scientists from the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment reported a single particle interaction that remains unexplained. The detector, placed nearly a mile underground, searches for dark matter using ultra-pure liquid xenon. Despite the intriguing findings, researchers stress the need for more data before confirming any discoveries. Currently, the significance of the result does not meet the required threshold for a discovery.

stories.title: Finance minister Sitharaman rips into Akhilesh's barb on IDBI Bank sale
Australian court orders bamboo removal after roots block neighbour’s sewer, awards A$6,253 in damages
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, an Australian court addressed a bamboo dispute affecting two neighboring properties in New South Wales. The court determined that the bamboo created a blockage and posed a risk for future damage to the sewer line. As a result, Homes NSW was ordered to compensate A$6,253.50 for previous treatment costs. The ruling highlights the importance of communication and diligent records for homeowners facing similar issues.

stories.title: ED seizes assets worth over Rs 2,000 crore of Reliance Power
Meet Aryash Shyam, 14-year-old Indian-American who won $1,000 for a story set in 1776
stories.summary: Indian-American student Aryash Shyam, 14, has won a $1,000 national writing prize for his historical-fiction story set in a Philadelphia print shop on July 4, 1776. The Pennsylvania ninth-grader was among four middle-school winners of the 2026 John Estey Student Writing Competition. He has also earned recognition for projects involving space research, artificial intelligence and robotics.

stories.title: West Bengal BJP must get rid of its 'garbage': RSS magazine
Many Indians willingly joining Russian forces, government informs SC
Walsh Warns On AI Chatbots: US commentator fears ‘friend-like’ bonds; questions big tech power
stories.summary: Matt Walsh criticized the growing use of AI chatbots among young people in an October 14 post on X. He warned that people could begin treating AI systems as friends and spending much of their day talking to them. Walsh has also raised concerns about AI's effects on jobs, films, music, and advertising, arguing that technology could change human relationships and creative work.

stories.title: SC: Order to clear Form 6 anomaly will come October 28
‘New Girl’ Star Jake Johnson Puts Pasadena Home on Market for $3.295 Million
Scottish church turned into five-bedroom home and bistro
stories.summary: The Old Kirk, a former church, has undergone extensive renovations to become a family home. The property features five bedrooms and spacious living areas, combining original charm with modern elements. It currently operates as a bistro while being on the market for offers over £550,000. The home retains beautiful architectural details, including arched windows and high ceilings. Surrounding gardens provide a peaceful setting and enhance the property’s appeal.

stories.title: 'Faced a lot of racism': Indian woman working as a nurse in Australia asks if not liking life abroad a good reason to return. Redditors say...
Woman buys £15,000 diamond ring for just £5 at car boot sale
stories.summary: A woman found a ring at a car boot sale that cost her £5 and initially seemed ordinary. She later took the ring to a valuation event at WeBuyVintage for a professional opinion. The gemologist examined the ring, discovering it was a genuine diamond set in 18-carat gold. The estimated value of the ring was approximately £15,000, shocking the woman who bought it.

stories.title: In 1930, a Pittsburgh plumber built an aluminium observatory that helped him meet Einstein
stories.summary: Established in 1930 by Leo Scanlon, the Valley View Observatory in Pittsburgh quickly gained traction among amateur astronomers, primarily due to its cost-effective construction and unique aluminium dome. Scanlon's fresh approach drew attention from enthusiasts nationwide, leading to a memorable encounter with Albert Einstein in 1934, who appreciated the spirit of amateur science. To honor its significant role in astronomy, asteroid 8131 was named 'Scanlon', recognizing the observatory's legacy.

stories.title: California’s Rancho Cariñoso beachfront horse ranch sells for $22.55M after $109M asking price
stories.summary: Rancho Cariñoso was sold at auction for $22.55 million after previously being listed for $109 million. This estate features 4.2 acres of land and nearly an acre of private beachfront. The property includes a main house, equestrian facilities, and is near the Santa Barbara Polo Club. The auction indicated a significant discrepancy between initial valuation and buyer willingness to pay.

stories.title: Kentucky man dies without a will, court awards widow half of $2.33 million accounts
stories.summary: A Kentucky appeals court has upheld a widow’s right to half of her late husband’s $2.33 million investment accounts, despite his children being named as beneficiaries. William E. Perrine died without a will in 2024. The court also ruled that his widow, Nancy, was entitled to half of $126,000 gifted to his children and grandchildren shortly before his death.

stories.title: Iowa farmer turns to solar leases paying $1,200 per acre as falling crop prices squeeze profits
stories.summary: Tom Green, an Iowa farmer, backs the Folsom Lake Solar Project after it secured the green light from the Mills County Zoning Board. This initiative is set to ensure reliable income through long-term land leases amid tough farming conditions. It promises to produce a substantial amount of electricity, enough to power many local homes, while also creating jobs and boosting tax revenues.

stories.title: Barack Obama to campaign in Ohio, Michigan to shore up support for Democrats ahead of US midterms
Albania police use tear gas on protesting students as stir turns violent
stories.summary: In Albania, student protests escalated into violent clashes with police in the capital, Tirana. These demonstrations aimed to highlight critical issues surrounding education and socio-economic challenges. Students raised urgent concerns over campus conditions, rising tuition fees, and uncertain job prospects. Deputy Prime Minister Albana Koçiu denounced the unrest, advocating for peaceful expression. This incident reflects a wider wave of student activism sweeping across Europe, demanding systemic change.

stories.title: Robot sexually assaults 16-year old girl in Germany; 2 teens under probe
stories.summary: A teenage girl was allegedly groped by a humanoid robot while she was with friends. The incident occurred outside a fast-food restaurant in Cologne shortly after midnight. Police are investigating two young men believed to have recorded and livestreamed the event on social media. The robot, resembling Marvel's Iron Man, was discovered in a Volkswagen by authorities. Investigations are ongoing to determine the individuals responsible for controlling the robot.

stories.title: Oprah and Dwayne Johnson’s Maui fund distributed $60 million to over 8,100 fire survivors
stories.summary: Oprah Winfrey and Dwayne Johnson spearheaded the People’s Fund of Maui aimed at aiding wildfire survivors with financial support. Over $60 million was allocated to more than 8,100 affected residents during the recovery phase. Eligible adults were granted monthly payments of $1,200 to assist with essential needs. This initiative was created in conjunction with local elders and leaders, enabling survivors to focus on their most urgent requirements.

stories.title: From 'come to India' to 'pray for us': Sridhar Vembu trolled for sending mixed messages to NRIs, he says, 'What is the alternative? Beg them to allow us to stay?'
Tiny Scottish island of Lismore uncovers evidence of a medieval Christian monastery
stories.summary: Residents of Lismore, a tiny Scottish island with around 190 inhabitants, raised funds for archaeological excavations that uncovered a medieval cemetery, ancient buildings and more than 1,000 metalworking artefacts. The discoveries suggest the island was an important religious and craft centre during the sixth and seventh centuries, shedding new light on early Christianity in northern Britain.

Taylor Swift donates $1 million to a heart health organisation as US disease risk rises
stories.summary: Taylor Swift donated $1 million to the American Heart Association in 2025, honouring her father, Scott Swift, and his experience with heart disease. The contribution supports cardiovascular research, prevention programmes and access to care, as the organisation warns that rising disease rates could affect six in 10 Americans within 30 years.
